raw_response:
*Sitting down with tea, thinking out loud*

Forty years on this land. My father planted here, and his father. Ten point nine mu — not big, but it's mine to manage. The wife and I, plus the elder boy when he's home from the city, that's the work force. Younger son and his wife work in Handan, they send money sometimes but we can't count on it for farming cash.

I split the land the way I've done it for years. About 7 mu on wheat-maize rotation — that's our food security, and the grain market is steady enough. The other 3.9 mu stays in cotton. Cotton prices aren't what they were ten years ago, but I know cotton, I've got the sprayer, and switching to vegetables would mean learning everything over at 58. Not worth it.

**Wheat (already in the ground since last October):**
Planted Jimai 22 again — good variety, my neighbor Old Zhang has been using it too, holds up in dry springs. Put down a compound fertilizer before planting, about 40 kg/mu of 15-15-15, so that's 6 kg each of N, P, K from the base. The extension fellow at the agri-service station said topdress 10-12 kg urea at jointing, but I usually do a bit more — maybe 15 kg — because the ground here is sandy-loam and loses nitrogen fast. Already irrigated once before winter (winter water is important here), again at greening in March. Still need jointing irrigation and one more at grain-filling if May stays dry. Expecting maybe 450 kg/mu — last year I got 430 because of the late frost.

**Maize (planting right after wheat harvest in June):**
Tight turnaround — I rent the rotary tiller from the village cooperative, one day to turn the stubble, then no-till plant the maize with the two-row seeder I share with my cousin. Zhengdan 958 or similar hybrid, I buy fresh seed every year, no saving hybrid seed — that's one thing the extension training got through to me years ago. One-shot fertilizer with the seed, about 40 kg/mu of a slow-release compound. If the summer rains come I won't need to irrigate at all; if July is dry I'll pump once at tasseling. Expecting around 500 kg/mu.

**Cotton (planting now, end of April):**
This is the crop that takes the most work and the most money. Bt cotton seed — have to buy each year, 70 yuan a mu just for seed. Plastic mulch for early warming, my wife lays that with me. Fertilizer is the tricky one — cotton eats a lot but if you over-do nitrogen you get all leaves and no bolls. I put down about 35 kg of compound before mulching, then side-dress urea at first flower, maybe 12 kg. Pesticide is the killer cost — aphids early, bollworm later, spider mites in August. Probably spray 6-8 times over the season. Expecting 250 kg lint/mu if the weather cooperates. Cotton picking is all family labor, mostly the wife and me, takes all of September into October, pick over pick.

Cash this year is tight. I've got about 6,000 yuan saved for inputs from last year's sales. Cotton inputs alone will run close to 2,400 yuan for 3.9 mu. Wheat topdress and the maize package will be another 2,500 or so. Pesticide and fuel on top. Tight, but we'll manage — always do.
